serialization: strict newline-delimited ASCII handshake and request-response records
ownership: each process owns its buffers; the Go host owns child lifecycle, checkpoint state, and timeout authority
nullability: not applicable to the serialized protocol
containment: Rust panic or process failure terminates the child and cannot unwind into Go; replacement requires explicit policy
timeout: Go context terminates the child at the declared deadline; the mutation corpus verifies bounded cancellation latency
cancellation: context cancellation kills the child process and prevents additional requests
retry: no automatic process retry; controlled replacement resumes from an identity-verified checkpoint
version_negotiation: exact READY V2 rust-authority-v2 handshake and exact V2 request token
malformed_input: unknown version, missing fields, extra fields, out-of-range values, partial writes, misordered IDs, mismatched values, and oversized lines reject
compatibility_policy: exact protocol schema, authority source, system contract, and checkpoint identities before restore
unknown_conditions: network transport behavior not exercised by subprocess study
